summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of chronic nausea, gastroparesis, and back pain was admitted for acute nausea and vomiting that began after taking morning medications on an empty stomach. She was not in diabetic ketoacidosis, and labs showed no evidence of infection, obstruction, or metabolic derangement. Her symptoms improved with IV fluids, antiemetics, and continuation of H. pylori treatment. Back pain, exacerbated by retching, resolved with her home regimen of acetaminophen and tramadol. She was discharged home with visiting nursing services, transportation support, and a new prescription for on-demand Zofran ODT for nausea, with stable diabetes management and follow-up plans.
